SEARCH
Package org.checkerframework.framework.stubifier

Class BinaryStubWriter

java.lang.Object
org.checkerframework.framework.stubifier.BinaryStubWriter
public class BinaryStubWriter extends Object
Writes parsed stub compilation units into the compressed binary stub format read by org.checkerframework.framework.stub.BinaryStubReader. The output is a GZIP-compressed file (see writeTo(java.io.File)), conventionally named with the BIN_SUFFIX suffix (.bin.gz, e.g. OUTPUT_FILENAME). Used at build time for the annotated JDK (via JavaStubifier) and for the built-in checker stub files (via BinaryStubFileGenerator).

This extracts annotations structurally from class, interface, enum, annotation-type, and record declarations and their members — including type-parameter bound annotations, enum constants, annotation-type members, and record components (including an explicit canonical constructor's parameter annotation overrides) — and writes them into a dense binary format optimized for rapid loading without parsing overhead at checker startup.

Name resolution and member filtering deliberately mirror the text parser ( AnnotationFileParser): private declarations are skipped, annotation names resolve through explicit imports, java.lang, and asterisk imports, and @CFComment is dropped.

A writer constructed with omitUnannotatedMembers drops field records that carry no annotations and demotes unannotated method records to bare presence-only signature entries (see BinaryStubWriter.ClassRecord.presenceOnlyMethodSigs); that is correct only for the annotated JDK. See that field's documentation. Equivalence is enforced by BinaryStubDiffChecker; run NullnessBinaryStubDiffTest after changing this class.

A writer constructed with skipUnloadableAnnotations drops, rather than fails on, an annotation whose @Target cannot be read; see that field's documentation for the trade-off this accepts.

    • MAGIC

      public static final int MAGIC
      Magic number identifying the Checker Framework binary stub format (CF + JDK: 0xCF non-ASCII marker byte, 'J' 0x4A, 'D' 0x44, 'K' 0x4B). This is the canonical definition; org.checkerframework.framework.stub.BinaryStubData#MAGIC references it.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • VERSION

      public static final short VERSION
      Format version of the binary stub file. This is the canonical definition; org.checkerframework.framework.stub.BinaryStubData#VERSION references it. Increment whenever the binary format changes, and add a line here.

      Version history:

      • 1: the first format (#1853).
      • 2: records the length and SHA-256 digest of the source stub file, for the staleness check of user-supplied -Astubs files (#1967).
      • 3: markers for plain wildcards ? (TYPE_ANNO_UNBOUNDED_WILDCARD); the annotations on a wildcard with a bound are written at the path of its other bound.
      • 4: constant expressions as trees of operations, evaluated by the reader; int and float literals keep their types; a simple name lists the classes that static imports can import it from; string values are unescaped.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • BUNDLE_MAGIC

      public static final int BUNDLE_MAGIC
      Magic number identifying a binary stub bundle: a container of several per-file binary stubs for a whole -Astubs directory, written by BinaryStubFileGenerator's --bundle mode and read by org.checkerframework.framework.stub.BinaryStubBundle. Distinct from MAGIC so that a reader can tell a bundle from a per-file binary stub whose name collides with it (see BUNDLE_SUFFIX) and ignore it rather than fail.
      See Also:

    • BUNDLE_VERSION

      public static final short BUNDLE_VERSION
      Format version of the binary stub bundle container. Independent of VERSION: a bundle entry is itself a complete, ordinarily-versioned binary stub blob, so this version covers only the container (entry count and the path/length framing around each entry).

    • BUNDLE_SUFFIX

      public static final String BUNDLE_SUFFIX
      File-name suffix appended to a source stub directory's name to name the bundle covering it (e.g. a -Astubs directory named mystubs → sibling file mystubs.astub.bin.gz). Unlike BIN_SUFFIX, which is appended to a file that already ends in .astub, a directory name has no such extension to begin with, so this suffix spells it out. This is the canonical definition; org.checkerframework.framework.stub.BinaryStubBundle#SUFFIX references it.

    • TYPE_ANNO_UNBOUNDED_WILDCARD

      public static final int TYPE_ANNO_UNBOUNDED_WILDCARD
      Annotation-pool index that makes a type annotation a marker: it carries no annotation, and its type path locates a plain wildcard ?, one without a bound or an annotation. The reader gives that wildcard the annotations of the bounds of its type variable's declaration, as the text parser does ( AnnotationFileParser.annotateUnannotatedUnboundedWildcard). Negative, so it is never a pool index, and not IGNORED, which is never written.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • CF_COMMENT

      public static final String CF_COMMENT
      Fully-qualified name of org.checkerframework.framework.qual.CFComment, which is never written to the binary format; see BinaryStubWriter.AnnotationPool.addAnnotation(com.github.javaparser.ast.expr.AnnotationExpr, com.github.javaparser.ast.CompilationUnit, org.checkerframework.framework.stubifier.BinaryStubWriter). BinaryStubDiffChecker filters the same annotation out of the text-parsed side.

      Must stay a compile-time constant (hence the literal, rather than CFComment.class.getCanonicalName()): javac interns it, so the reference-equality check in BinaryStubDiffChecker works.

      See Also:

    • setSourceFingerprint

      public void setSourceFingerprint(byte[] sourceBytes)
      Records the source .astub file this writer's output is generated from, so writeTo(java.io.File) embeds a fingerprint that a reader can use to detect a stale binary. Only BinaryStubFileGenerator calls this: the annotated JDK and other output of JavaStubifier are never checked for staleness this way, and leave it unset.
      Parameters:
      sourceBytes - the source file's raw content

    • processStubUnit

      public void processStubUnit(List<com.github.javaparser.ast.CompilationUnit> cus)
      Processes the compilation units of one stub file. A stub file may contain multiple package sections, which the stub parser represents as multiple compilation units; the text parser resolves names against the imports of the first unit only (see AnnotationFileParser.getImportedAnnotations), and this method does the same.
      Parameters:
      cus - the compilation units of the stub file, in order

    • writeTo

      public void writeTo(OutputStream out) throws IOException
      Writes the accumulated class records and constant pool to the given stream in a compressed binary format, exactly as writeTo(File) does. Lets a caller assemble several writers' output in memory (see BinaryStubFileGenerator's --bundle mode) instead of writing each one to its own file.
      Parameters:
      out - the stream to write to; closed by this method
      Throws:
      IOException - if writing to the stream fails
